DependencyClause.description:
#DependencyClause is a single dependency clause: an OR-group of one or more
alternative package IDs, following Debian's dependency syntax. A bare
dependency is a singleton array (["some-id"]), not a bare string — the
original `string | [...string]` disjunction rendered as
`"type": ["string", "array"]` with `"oneOf": [{}, {}]` in the generated CRD
schema, which is not valid Kubernetes JSONSchemaProps (type must be a single
string) and would fail to apply.

screenId.description: screenId is the screen this CTA navigates to

linkText.description: linkText is the visible anchor text

type.description: type is an optional link category hint

GrotGuideOption.description: #GrotGuideOption is a single branch from a grot guide question screen

screenId.description: screenId is the screen this option navigates to

GrotGuideScreen.description:
#GrotGuideScreen is a single screen in a grot guide decision tree.
Like #Block, it uses a "fat struct" pattern: `type` discriminates between
question screens (which carry `options`) and result screens (which carry
`body` and `links`).

body.description: body is the result screen prose (result screens only)

id.description: id is the screen identifier referenced by ctas and options

links.description: links are related links shown on a result screen (result screens only)

options.description: options are the branches offered by a question screen (question screens only)

type.description:
type is the screen type discriminator
Valid values: "question", "result"

GrotGuideWelcome.description: #GrotGuideWelcome is the entry screen of a grot guide decision tree

ctas.description: ctas are the entry points into the decision tree

GuideStats.description:
#GuideStats is the guide's computed block statistics, stamped onto the
manifest at build time. It is the denominator for completion percentages,
and the reason it lives here rather than in additionalFields is so a
consumer holding a resolved manifest reads the same path whether the guide
came from bundled/CDN content or from this app platform.

Every member is REQUIRED and none carries a default. A defaulted count of 0
is indistinguishable from a guide genuinely measured as having no blocks, so
a partial or malformed stamp would be silently accepted as real data and go
on to divide by it. Requiring all five means a partial stamp is rejected
(422) instead. The whole object stays optional on #Manifest — see there.

Mirrors the app's emitted shape (grafana-pathfinder-app,
src/types/guide-stats.schema.ts / src/lib/guide-stats/summary.ts).

blockCount.description: blockCount is the completion denominator: counted blocks, containers excluded.

completableBlockCount.description:
completableBlockCount is the number of counted blocks carrying a completion
affordance.

finalCompletablePosition.description:
finalCompletablePosition is the position of the last completable block, 0
when there is none. Equal to blockCount when the final counted block is
completable, which is the signal that the guide needs no "Mark as complete"
button at its foot.

sectionCount.description:
sectionCount is the number of section containers. Authoring insight;
deliberately not in the denominator.

version.description:
version is the version of the stamped stats object. Bump it when the
COUNTING RULE changes, or when these fields change shape — the rule being
the load-bearing trigger, because a rule change leaves the shapes untouched
while restating the denominator of every already-stamped manifest and every
percentage already recorded against it.

NOT a content version: it says nothing about whether the guide changed.
Not resourceVersion either — it has nothing to do with the stored object.

Manifest.description:
#Manifest carries package-repository metadata for grouping, sequencing, and
(future) dependency-graph participation. Scoped intentionally: fields with no
current consumer (recommender targeting, E2E test-environment routing) are
left out until something in this app platform actually reads them.

additionalFields.description:
additionalFields is an escape hatch for manifest data not yet promoted to a
typed field above. #Manifest itself can't be made open-world — CUE's
pattern-constraint mechanism ([string]: _) only preserves unknown fields
(x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true) when applied to a field's own
object type, not to the containing struct; applying it to #Manifest directly
silently widened other fields' types (e.g. `type` lost its enum) without
achieving passthrough. This mirrors grafana-app-sdk's own
SchemaWithOperatorState.status.additionalFields convention. Promoting a key
out of here into a real field on #Manifest is always additive and safe.

author.description: author identifies who owns this guide/path/journey.

category.description: category is a free-form grouping label for browsing/filtering.

depends.description: depends is a CNF (AND of ORs) list of package IDs this package depends on.

description.description: description is a short human-readable summary shown in listings.

milestones.description: milestones is the ordered list of member package IDs for "path"/"journey" types.

repository.description: repository identifies the provenance of this package.

stats.description:
stats is the guide's computed block statistics, stamped at build time.

Optional with NO default: guides written before this field existed must
survive the addition and simply carry no stats until something saves them
again. Absent stats means "not measured"; it must never be forgeable into a
zero-valued measurement. When present, all five members are required — see
#GuideStats.

tracks.description:
tracks is a list of named, additional guide sequences alongside the
default sequence in milestones. See #Track. Meaningful only for
type: "path" (RFC §6.1) but not restricted to it at this schema
layer — see AGENTS.md's "#Track naming and scope".

type.description: type discriminates a standalone guide from an ordered group of guides.

NestedBlock.description:
#NestedBlock is used for blocks within section/collapsible/assistant/conditional
blocks to avoid infinite recursion in the schema. It carries the same fields as
#Block; only its own child arrays are left untyped, which the CRD generator
renders as `x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields` so deeper nesting is passed
through rather than pruned.

Track.description:
#Track is a named, independently-ordered guide sequence for a learning
path — never a subset of milestones. See AGENTS.md's "#Track naming and scope".

description.description: description is a short human-readable summary shown in listings.

guides.description:
guides is this track's own ordered list of member package IDs, same
shape as milestones. Non-empty per the RFC but unenforced here — see
AGENTS.md.

label.description: label is the human-facing name for this track.

trackId.description: trackId identifies this track within its manifest's tracks list.

blocks.description: blocks is the array of content blocks that make up the guide

id.description: id is the unique identifier for the guide

manifest.description:
manifest carries package-repository metadata (grouping, sequencing,
dependencies) so this guide can participate as a package alongside
bundled and CDN content. Absent for legacy content-only guides.

schemaVersion.description: schemaVersion is the version of the guide schema format

status.description:
status is the publication status of the guide
Valid values: "draft", "published"

title.description: title is the human-readable title of the guide

additionalFields.description: additionalFields is reserved for future use

operatorStates.description:
operatorStates is a map of operator ID to operator state evaluations.
Any operator which consumes this kind SHOULD add its state evaluation information to this field.

descriptiveState.description: descriptiveState is an optional more descriptive state field which has no requirements on format

details.description: details contains any extra information that is operator-specific

lastEvaluation.description: lastEvaluation is the ResourceVersion last evaluated

state.description:
state describes the state of the lastEvaluation.
It is limited to three possible states for machine evaluation.

completedAt.description:
completedAt is the ISO 8601 timestamp of WHEN THE USER COMPLETED the guide
(client-supplied; preserved unchanged across offline/queued retries).
OPTIONAL: absent while the guide is in progress. Set exactly once, when
completionPercent reaches 100, and never cleared afterwards.

completionPercent.description:
completionPercent is the highest completion percentage (0-100) reached in
this attempt; 100 means the guide is complete. NOTE: the generator emits
this as uint64 in Go and drops the >=0 minimum from the CRD JSON; the <=100
upper bound is preserved. Accepted codegen quirk — do not fight the generator.

durationSeconds.description: durationSeconds is the time from first view to completion.

guideCategory.description:
guideCategory is the category of the guide.
Valid values: "interactive", "documentation", "learning-journey".

guideId.description:
guideId is the guide identifier WITHIN its source (not globally unique on
its own; the durable guide identity is the pair (guideSource, guideId)).

guideSource.description:
guideSource is the provenance of the guide (= the resolving repository).
v1 values: "bundled" | "app-platform" | "remote-repo:<name>". The durable
guide identity is the pair (guideSource, guideId). Kept as a free-form
string so new sources need no schema bump. Distinct from `source` below:
guideSource is WHERE the guide came from, `source` is HOW it was completed.

guideTitle.description:
guideTitle is the denormalized guide title, snapshotted at write time so
dashboards remain readable years later even if the guide is renamed or
removed (RFC §6.10).

orgId.description:
orgId is the Grafana organization identifier the write originated from,
making the per-record org context explicit rather than implicit (RFC §7.1).

pathId.description: pathId is the learning path ID (empty string if none).

platform.description:
platform is the platform where the guide was completed.
Valid values: "oss", "cloud".

recordedAt.description:
recordedAt is the ISO 8601 timestamp of WHEN THE LAST WRITE LANDED
(authoritative), re-stamped on every write. Distinct from completedAt: a
queued retry that lands hours later still reports the true completion time
in completedAt while recordedAt reflects when the record was last written
(RFC §7.1).

schemaVersion.description:
schemaVersion is the CompletionRecord spec schema version (>= 1). Separate
from the CRD apiVersion so we can correct schema mistakes without an
API-version bump (RFC §7.1).

source.description:
source is HOW the completion happened: "objectives" (earned by completing all
objectives), "manual" (marked complete by the user), or "skipped" (user used
the "skip remaining" affordance). Distinct from guideSource above, which is
WHERE the guide came from (RFC §7.1, §6.11).

stackNamespace.description:
stackNamespace is the App Platform namespace (per-stack scope) the record was
written into. The CRD is namespaced per-stack, but §7.1 requires that linkage
explicit on the record for future cross-stack analysis/export.

userDisplayName.description:
userDisplayName is the denormalized display name, snapshotted at write time
so dashboards remain readable years later even after the user is renamed or
deleted (RFC §6.10).

userId.description:
userId is the stable, rename-safe user identifier the trusted writer derives
from the Grafana ID token. Logins are mutable, so this is the durable join
key for "everything this user did" (RFC §7.1).

userLogin.description: userLogin is the Grafana user login at the time of the write.

additionalFields.description: additionalFields is reserved for future use

operatorStates.description:
operatorStates is a map of operator ID to operator state evaluations.
Any operator which consumes this kind SHOULD add its state evaluation information to this field.

descriptiveState.description: descriptiveState is an optional more descriptive state field which has no requirements on format

details.description: details contains any extra information that is operator-specific

lastEvaluation.description: lastEvaluation is the ResourceVersion last evaluated

state.description:
state describes the state of the lastEvaluation.
It is limited to three possible states for machine evaluation.

acceptedTermsAndConditions.description:
acceptedTermsAndConditions records acceptance or refusal of the
recommender terms. Absence uses the platform-specific client default.

devModeEnabled.description:
devModeEnabled is the instance-level gate for developer surfaces. A user
sees dev features only when this is true AND that user has opted in via
their browser-local, user-scoped storage. Replaces the old jsonData pair
(`devMode` + `devModeUserIds`); the per-user half moved out of this
tenant-scoped resource entirely.

disableAutoCollapse.description: disableAutoCollapse stops sections collapsing as they complete.

enableAiAutoHeal.description:
enableAiAutoHeal allows the AI write path to repair guides:
this writes on the user's behalf and requires explicit admin opt-in.

enableAssistantDevMode.description:
enableAssistantDevMode mocks Grafana Assistant availability so the
integration can be exercised on OSS. Only meaningful when devModeEnabled
is true and the viewing user has opted in.

enableAutoDetection.description: enableAutoDetection turns on automatic detection of interactive elements.

enableCodaTerminal.description:
enableCodaTerminal shows the Coda terminal UI. The VM backend and its
credentials live in the separate grafana-coda-app plugin, which owns its
own settings.

enableKioskMode.description: enableKioskMode enables the kiosk guide-catalogue presentation surface.

enableTwoTabController.description:
enableTwoTabController enables the live-tab executor, which drives the
user's authenticated Grafana DOM and requires explicit admin opt-in.

guidedStepTimeout.description: guidedStepTimeout is the per-step budget in milliseconds.

interceptGlobalDocsLinks.description:
interceptGlobalDocsLinks routes Grafana docs links into the panel.
Experimental opt-in.

kioskRulesUrl.description:
kioskRulesUrl is an optional rules document for kiosk mode. Empty string
means "none".

openPanelOnLaunch.description:
openPanelOnLaunch opens the docs panel on page load. Experimental opt-in;
may be overridden by a feature toggle.

pathfinderEnabled.description: pathfinderEnabled is the org opt-out; absence enables Pathfinder unless the remote kill switch is off.

peerjsHost.description: peerjsHost is the PeerJS signalling host used by live sessions.

peerjsKey.description:
peerjsKey is the PeerJS application key. Not a secret: PeerJS keys scope a
signalling namespace, they do not authenticate. Anything genuinely secret
belongs in secureJsonData, which this kind deliberately does not hold.

peerjsPort.description:
peerjsPort is the PeerJS signalling port. The exclusive upper bound
preserves the limit in generated OpenAPI; see AGENTS.md codegen notes.

peerjsSecure.description: peerjsSecure selects wss/https for the signalling connection.

recommenderServiceUrl.description:
recommenderServiceUrl is the recommender API base URL. The client still
validates this against ALLOWED_RECOMMENDER_DOMAINS before use — an
arbitrary string here must not become an arbitrary fetch target.

requirementsCheckTimeout.description:
requirementsCheckTimeout is the per-requirement check budget in
milliseconds. Bounded to keep a bad value from hanging a guide.

schemaVersion.description:
schemaVersion labels the spec format, separate from the CRD apiVersion.
Default 1 accepts sparse third-party creates that omit the version;
it does not prove the writer understood v1. No reader branches on it
today. Clients preserve it on updates; future migrations must not
use this default as evidence of explicit client version support.

termsVersion.description:
termsVersion is the terms version that was accepted, so a new version can
re-prompt.

tutorialUrl.description:
tutorialUrl is an optional override for the bundled tutorial index.
Empty string means "use the built-in default".

additionalFields.description: additionalFields is reserved for future use

operatorStates.description:
operatorStates is a map of operator ID to operator state evaluations.
Any operator which consumes this kind SHOULD add its state evaluation information to this field.

descriptiveState.description: descriptiveState is an optional more descriptive state field which has no requirements on format

details.description: details contains any extra information that is operator-specific

lastEvaluation.description: lastEvaluation is the ResourceVersion last evaluated

state.description:
state describes the state of the lastEvaluation.
It is limited to three possible states for machine evaluation.

acceptCompletionsFrom.description:
acceptCompletionsFrom is the earliest completion that counts
toward this obligation. Absent credits any prior completion.

assignedAt.description:
assignedAt is the ISO 8601 timestamp of when this obligation was
incurred. Written once, never modified.

assignedBy.description:
assignedBy is the assigning authority — which Learning Admin, or
the group acting as one. Free-form; no identifier format is
prescribed. Absent is allowed.

dueAt.description:
dueAt is when completions after this are late. Soft by definition:
an overdue obligation is displayed as overdue and never locked
out. Absent means no deadline.

lifecycle.description:
lifecycle is "active" or "withdrawn" — the only part of an
obligation that ever changes. Records are never deleted.

ruleId.description:
ruleId is the authored assignment rule's stable slug, stamped into
every record. It is the addressing key for withdrawal.

ruleRevision.description:
ruleRevision is the specific rule revision that produced this
record, so an obligation is auditable back to a decision.
Free-form (a git SHA, a generation, a tag). Absent if the
writer has none.

schemaVersion.description:
schemaVersion is the Assignment spec schema version (>= 1).
Separate from the CRD apiVersion so a schema mistake can be
corrected without an API-version bump.

targetId.description:
targetId is the assigned thing within targetType's namespace.
For targetType "path" this is the learning path id.

targetSource.description:
targetSource is the provenance of targetId when that identity is
a pair, matching CompletionRecord's (guideSource, guideId).
Absent for paths, which have no source in that sense.

targetType.description:
targetType discriminates the namespace targetId lives in:
"github-visualize" can be both a path and a guide. Adding a
value later is an enum expansion, so existing rows stay valid.
Never default it — absent-means-path would collide with a mixed
population, and a single-value CUE constraint emits no enum.

trackId.description:
trackId qualifies a path target to a specific named track.
Absent means the whole path. Meaningless for a non-path
targetType; leave it absent.

userId.description:
userId is the assigned person, in the stack's canonical subject
vocabulary: the typed ID-token subject (such as "user:27"), the
same one CompletionRecord uses so obligation and fulfilment join
without an identity bridge. Logins are mutable; this is not.

withdrawnAt.description:
withdrawnAt is the ISO 8601 timestamp of the active → withdrawn
transition. Absent when lifecycle is active. A nested
{state, at} object would prevent either field becoming a
metadata.label.

additionalFields.description: additionalFields is reserved for future use

operatorStates.description:
operatorStates is a map of operator ID to operator state evaluations.
Any operator which consumes this kind SHOULD add its state evaluation information to this field.

satisfied.description:
satisfied caches the evaluation of this obligation's criteria
against the subject's completions, for consumers that cannot
join against CompletionRecord. Absent means not yet evaluated,
which is distinct from false (evaluated and unmet).
